plain.text: Jacob came to a well in the east where shepherds gathered with their flocks. He asked about Laban, and they said, "Here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep." Jacob rolled the stone away from the well and watered Laban's sheep. He kissed Rachel and wept aloud, and told her he was Rebekah's son. She ran to tell her father, and Laban welcomed Jacob warmly.

After a month, Laban asked what wages Jacob wanted. Laban had two daughters, Leah, the older, and Rachel, who was lovely in form and beautiful. Jacob loved Rachel and offered to work seven years for her. The seven years seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her. Laban held a wedding feast, but that night he brought Leah to Jacob instead. In the morning Jacob found it was Leah and said, "What have you done to me? Why have you deceived me?" Laban said it was not their custom to marry the younger before the older, but he could have Rachel too after the wedding week, in return for seven more years of work. Jacob agreed. He loved Rachel more than Leah.

When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, he enabled her to have children, but Rachel was childless. Leah had Reuben, hoping her husband would love her now; then Simeon, because the LORD heard she was unloved; then Levi, hoping her husband would become attached to her. Then she had Judah, and said, "This time I will praise the LORD."

summary.bigIdea: The deceiver Jacob is deceived by Laban, and God sees and cares for unloved Leah.
points: Jacob meets Rachel at a well and loves her.
Laban tricks Jacob into marrying Leah first.
God sees that Leah is unloved and gives her sons; at Judah's birth she says, "This time I will praise the LORD."
summary.reflection: God noticed Leah when she felt unloved. Do you know that God sees you too?
